blocks.text: Yes. You can see above that as well that she was 36 weeks and 2 days corrected gestation by then, so she's almost a

blocks.text: term baby and had been stable for the weeks beforehand. And she'd received one dose of phenobarbitone for the seizures.

blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: In terms of feeds, she was taking 165ml per kilogram per day of expressed breast milk or donor-expressed breast milk every 3 hours by either NG tube or bottle, which is a good sign. She was fully enterally fed and taking some bottles, which is excellent.
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Her weight was going up and the most recent weight was 2.144 kilograms. There had been some concerns about her weight gain, but to have gained some weight, particularly even after that episode, was positive and -- I think Mr Murphy might have to scroll down a bit.
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Can you go back up to the last one?
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Mr Murphy is actually over there.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Sorry.
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Don't worry about it. Mr Murphy is the man who's doing the screen.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: The CRP was 1, that's a normal level. So there's no evidence of infection on the blood tests. The antibiotics had been stopped by the team. We have a review time of 36 hours so they would have been stopped then prior to my ward round.

blocks.text: I examined [Baby J]. She was looking well, pink, active, handling well, her heart sounds were normal, no murmurs were heard. Her chest was clear to listen to the breath sounds. I have done a diagrammatic of her abdomen there, with her stoma on the left and the right.

blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: distal end of the two stomas that joined up. So one has got the stoma output coming out --
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: -- that's the ileostomy. blocks.text: Do you remember which fistula it was?

blocks.text: It's a long time ago, but in the way I've written that I suggest it was the mucous fistula, the stoma that we were recycling through.

blocks.text: But in any event --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, there's no concerns, yes.

blocks.text: Your plan, please?

blocks.text: To continue recycling the stoma contents through the mucous fistula and continue establishing feeds for [Baby J].
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Nothing more than that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, no.
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: You commented a moment or two ago about [Baby J]'s recovery by the afternoon of 27 November.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: How was she presenting on 29 November?

blocks.text: Thank you very much for coming and giving evidence this afternoon, Dr Brearey. You will be returning, I gather, to give further evidence in relation to another baby, so please don't talk to anyone about this case, any of the babies, anything to do with it, to anyone.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Okay, thank you.
blocks.speaker: BREAREY

blocks.text: Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (The witness withdrew)
My Lord, that leaves us some more statements to read, but no further witnesses this afternoon.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: About how long will it take?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: 15 or 20 minutes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: In those circumstances, shall we sit through for 15 or 20 minutes and then finish for the day? It seems to make better use of time. You're all still concentrating, I'm sure. Yes? Good.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Just because it's read, I remind you of what I've said more than once: it doesn't mean to say it's any less important than any other evidence. The important thing is it's agreed. Anything that is read to you is agreed evidence and I have said this before, I shall say it again, and I will say it again in the future: what you make of any piece of evidence is entirely for you and how it fits in with other evidence for you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Witness statement of MS CAROLINE OAKLEY (read)
My Lord, I'll begin at this stage with Caroline Oakley at page 5 of the bundle.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Caroline Oakley in a statement dated 2 March 2018 says this:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on baby [Baby J] and in particular her care on 27 November 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I was working on a night shift of the 26th into 27 November 2015 and was shift leader on this shift. The designated nurse for [Baby J] on the shift was Nicola Dennison.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As shift leader, I would not normally have an allocated baby to care for but if the unit was particularly busy I could find myself allocated a baby to look after.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have reviewed the nursing notes for this shift and can state I am not documented as having cared for [Baby J] on this shift, however I cannot categorically state I did not have anything to do with her care during the night. One of roles of shift leader is to help and support the team and I may have helped the designated nurse of [Baby J] during the night."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She moves on in more detail, my Lord, at page 6 in a second statement, dated 2 May 2019:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment further on my dealings with [Baby J] and particularly her care during the night shift of the 26th into 27 November 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "On 26 November 2015 at 19.30 hours, I commenced the night shift, which finishes at 08.00 hours the following morning, Friday the 27th.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As shift leader, I would not normally have been allocated a baby to look after as my role and responsibilities is to oversee the entire unit for that shift and to provide support and assistance whenever necessary. However, on occasions there have been occasions when the unit has been particularly busy and the shift leader would have been allocated a baby to care for. I cannot recall if I had a baby allocated.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "On this particular night I do not recall caring for [Baby J]. I have reviewed the nursing notes for the shift and can state that I do not appear to have had any involvement in [Baby J]'s care that night. The entries made on the nursing notes were completed by Nicola Dennison or Mary Griffith.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Nicola Dennison, a band 4 nursery nurse, was allocated the designated nurse for [Baby J] during the shift. It is documented by Nicola on the nursing notes that [Baby J] became unwell shortly after 04.00 hours and suddenly desaturated.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Having reviewed the nursing notes, it appears that Nicola Dennison and Mary Griffith have been responsible for the electronic entries on [Baby J]'s nursing notes that evening. It has been documented on the nursing notes by Nicola Dennison, timestamped at 07.49."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: And she quotes in particular the entry:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby J] was moved into nursery 2 for closer observations and plan to omit the 8 am feed."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: She returns to her statement:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "This entry would indicate that [Baby J], at the start of the shift, would have been in nursery room 3 or 4. I do vaguely remember from the notes. She was born at 32 weeks and was transferred to Alder Hey Children's Hospital and returned back to the Countess of Chester. [Baby J] had a stoma, which is where a piece of the bowel is removed and one end of the bowel is brought to the surface of the abdominal wall.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I do not recall having any involvement with [Baby J] on that night shift. I cannot remember what I would have been dealing with at the time of her collapse or where I was.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As the shift leader, there is nothing significant that stands out in my memory about that shift or what or who I was dealing with at the time of [Baby J]'s collapse. I don't recall the shift being busier than any other night shift. However, that doesn't mean it wasn't, I just cannot recall any of the details relating to this sudden collapse of [Baby J].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I cannot categorically state I did not have anything to do with her care at all that night. As shift leader I am there to provide support and help when needed. There is nothing about this shift that stands out in my memory."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of DR RACHEL CHANG (read)
Page 17, please, my Lord, next. A statement from Rachel Chang, dated 28 June 2018. Dr Chang says:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on baby [Baby J] and in particular her care on 27 November 2015. During this time I was an ST3 specialty training year 3 registrar working at the Countess of Chester Hospital having started my six-month placement in September 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "On this day I was working a day shift and conducted ward rounds on the neonatal unit. I assume I had been allocated to work on the NNU that day as my entry is first thing in the morning.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "My notes for [Baby J] start at 09.30 hours on 27 November 2015, so she would have been one of the first babies I had seen due to her being unwell overnight.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I noted that [Baby J] had no further seizures or abnormal movements since the event overnight/early morning and the only thing to note was there was still a bit of blood in her stoma. This had been in the previous 48 hours, which I thought may have been related to trauma as her stoma had been re-fed."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Re-feeding of stomas involves the insertion of a tube into her stoma, so this tubing can sometimes cause some minor trauma. I conducted a full examination of [Baby J], including an examination of her head, which is routine for children who have had seizures. We do this to ensure we exclude fluid build-up or swelling in the brain.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I also examined [Baby J]'s abdomen as this was one of her main areas of concern since birth. There was the potential that she
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: was getting infection from her abdomen after her surgery or from a potential new perforation which would make her unwell.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The examination showed that [Baby J] was off colour and had poor tone. It is likely to be related to the drugs that she had been given to stop her seizures. I noted that there possibly could be a problem with [Baby J]'s bowel after noticing a potential abnormality on an X-ray. This prompted me to ask the specialist at Alder Hey Children's Hospital, who had conducted the stoma surgery, to review these images.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The start of my notes detail a brief history of [Baby J], detailing that she was premature and was the second baby of twins. The sibling died prenatally due to twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome at 17 weeks. I also recapped the details of the stoma formation at Alder Hey Children's Hospital.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I break down my documented ward rounds into sections addressing each system of the baby that I review. My documented ward round is as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Vent (ventilation). [Baby J] was self-ventilating in air, which means she was breathing for herself. [Baby J] had mild intermittent respiratory distress in the morning. There had been no rise in her O2 requirements.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Fluids. [Baby J] was nil by mouth. At the time of my review she was receiving 180ml per kilogram per day of intravenous 10% dextrose and had 20ml per kilogram of sodium chloride overnight as a bolus when she had collapsed. Her urine output was not formally measured and there had been no excessive stoma losses that morning.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Cardiovascular system. [Baby J] was warm and well perfused peripherally but did look pale. Her capillary refill time was less than 2, which is normal. Her heart sounds was 1 plus 2 plus murmur. As I have not commented on this, I would assume this is normal for her.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Neuro. I have commented on her stiff positioning with apnoea, which I believe refers to what happened with [Baby J] overnight. I have also noted she was loaded with phenobarbitone, which is an anti-fitting drug and there had been no abnormal movements since its initiation. She had no further seizures when I was reviewing her.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Sepsis. [Baby J] had been screened for sepsis that morning. I noted that [Baby J] was on day 1 of antibiotics (teicoplanin and cefotaxime). [Baby J] had a Broviac line in situ, which can also
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: be a possible source of infection.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Gastrointestinal tract. I recorded that [Baby J] had one episode of GI issues in the previous day. That same day [Baby J] had been given a feed which came straight through to her proximal stoma, not absorbed. There had been some blood in her stoma output over the previous 24-48 hours too.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "This all appears to be me documenting what had happened with [Baby J] during the past 24 to 48 hours and there seemed to be no acute issues with the stoma at the time of my review.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Medication. [Baby J] was on day 1 of antibiotics (teicoplanin and cefotaxime). She was also having heparin which is a blood
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: thinner you put in a Broviac line to keep it open and patent and can therefore deliver medication.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby J] was nil by mouth at the time of my review but I have noted that when she was previously taking oral feeds, she had additional sodium supplements and expressed breast milk, fortifier daily.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Bloods. I have noted that [Baby J]'s bloods were taken at 07.00 hours that day and I have noted the results. The inflammation marker, CRP, was less than 1 which is low and reassuring and should be less than 5. Her white blood cell count was 8.1, which is normal. Her platelet count was 503, which is slightly high. Her haemoglobin was 78, which is lower than what would be liked, but a lower haemoglobin in babies on the NNU can be tolerated due to prematurity.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The haematocrit, the HCT, is the ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood. [Baby J]'s result was 0.2, which suggests the sample was dilute. This was likely to be related to the fact that she'd been given extra fluid into her veins as a bolus overnight.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Chest X-ray and abdominal X-ray. I commented that chest X-ray was rotated as [Baby J] may have moved or been malpositioned during the X-ray. There was 'nil focal', which means there was nothing abnormal to be seen. The abdominal X-ray showed an abnormal gas pattern around the stoma. I queried whether this was free air in the abdominal cavity (the right iliac fossa) which would possibly indicate air escaping into the abdomen from the bowel.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Blood gas. All of [Baby J]'s blood gas levels were good or acceptable. Her lactate was raised to 3.0. It should be ideally less than 2.0, but her previous seizures may have caused this rise.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "When I examined [Baby J] she was pale with reduced tone in her limbs, which is likely to be a side effect of the
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: phenobarbitone. She had no rashes and there were no skin breaks. Her head circumference was 29.4 centimetres and her anterior fontanelle was soft and equal.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Baby J] had clear lung fields when I listened. She had good air entry but had very occasional intermittent work of breathing. I examined her abdomen, documenting all of the stoma skin intact, but she was producing very green stool. [Baby J] handled well. There was no distension of her abdomen and I could still hear her bowel sounds, which would indicate her bowels were working.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Impression. I documented my questioning as to the source of the sepsis, querying whether it was the Broviac line [Baby J] had inserted or whether it was due to an abdominal source of sepsis such as a blockage, a perforation or an infection given that we were re-feeding remember stoma.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Plan. Moved forward I have documented a plan with regards to the short-term future care of [Baby J] which included: (1) add calcium/urea and electrolytes to bloods (which is routine in children having seizures); (2) a cranial ultrasound; (3) repeat
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: gas and full blood count in 4 hours (to prove/disprove the previous sample was dilute); (4) take fluids down to 165ml per
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: kilogram a day; (5) strict fluid balance; (6) discuss with surgeons at Alder Hey Children's Hospital at 10.15. After this phone call with the registrar at Alder Hey, they said they would review images with their consultant and call back.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "From my ward round review of [Baby J] and the history of her care I can say that she was more stable than she had been. She was clearly unwell but stable.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At 13.20 hours the same day I conducted a further review of [Baby J] with Dr Brearey. I wrote the notes for this review on his behalf. It was noted that nothing had changed significantly since my ward round review of [Baby J]. The blood results looked normal. Her repeat full blood count was still awaited. Dr Brearey made a clinical decision to request a blood transfusion and her blood group type was re-sent to ensure a match (which is routine).
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Alder Hey Children's Hospital were recontacted as they had not returned our earlier call. No discussions had taken place with the consultant at Alder Hey at that point but it was felt it was unlikely [Baby J]'s issues were abdominal in origin and an abdominal ultrasound was asked for [Baby J] and the completion of the review with Dr Brearey ended my involvement with [Baby J] on this particular day."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Witness statement of MS AILSA SIMPSON (read)
Thank you, my Lord. One more statement to read, please, at this stage. It's a statement of Ailsa Simpson, which is at page 1 of my Lord's bundle.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: In her statement dated 27 February 2018, she says this:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Further to the statement I have already provided to Cheshire Police regarding the ongoing investigation within the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital, I would like to add the following. I have been asked with reference to [Baby J] and in particular her care on 27 [November] 2015."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, this has been corrected since. It's a typographical error in the original.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "On this day I started a long day shift, which is 07.30 to 20.00 hours. I was allocated [Baby J] to look after as designated nurse. I remember [Baby J] and looking after her. I know she was a twin but the other twin died in utero/pre-birth.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: [Baby J] had two stomas and a necrotising enterocolitis inflammation of the bowel."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think that must be, frankly, in error:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I went to nursery 2 and had a verbal handover from Mary Griffith and Nicola Dennison who had been caring for [Baby J] overnight. Nicola and Mary told me that [Baby J] had been fine until approximately 4 am when she had begun to deteriorate and had two episodes during which she'd fitted. Dr Gibbs was also present and had prescribed phenobarbitone, an anti-fitting drug, for [Baby J]. I cannot recall if any other members of staff or babies in cots were also present at this time in nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I collected the medication from within a locked cupboard in nursery 1 and returned to [Baby J]. As per protocol, the medication was checked by Mary and I before it was administered to [Baby J]. I administered the medication to [Baby J] via her Broviac line which was sited in her chest. Mary and Nicola remained in or near to nursery 2 as I administered the medication. The phenobarbitone settled [Baby J] and she stabilised.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Dr Rachel Chang attended to [Baby J] as part of her ward rounds. She completed a full check of [Baby J] as per normal ward round visit.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I remained the designated nurse for [Baby J] for the entirety of the shift but [Baby J] remained stable throughout my shift. Cranial and abdominal ultrasounds were completed with nothing abnormal detected. Dr Chang liaised with [Nurse A], who was the on-call consultant that day, and then spoke with surgeons in Alder Hey and it was decided that [Baby J] should remain in the Chester with the current care, but if there was deterioration they would transfer her to Alder Hey.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I will have taken a break at some stage of the day but can't recall when that was or who took over the care of [Baby J] while I was away. I recall speaking with [Baby J]'s parents during the day and advising them as to the care of [Baby J] and what we were doing to help her. I remember them being very anxious, which is understandable considering what their child was going through.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "At approximately 19.30 hours that day I will have handed over the care of [Baby J] to the night staff. I can't recall exactly who was the designated nurse for [Baby J] that night, but the nursing notes show Lucy Letby as making entries immediately after my care, which is normally what happens when staff take over the care of a baby."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: My Lord, the next statement is simply the correction that I mentioned at the start with the dates. I'm not proposing to read that unless specifically asked to.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Well, no, it was clearly a typing error because it simply didn't make sense.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That concludes that bundle of reading.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Thank you very much. That then is as far as we can go today. Members of the jury, 10.30 tomorrow morning, please. Thank you very much. 10.30 tomorrow morning, please.
